facts.title: uncontrolled movement of P-7113 during an intrusive maintenance task

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.
Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had been bypassed, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next field verification that the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on P-7113 and TK-7104 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in managing hydrocarbon transfer and storage, specifically transferring hydrocarbon between vessels. P-7113 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during an intrusive maintenance task while the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 6 August 2010 an incident occurred on P-7113 and TK-7104 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during an intrusive maintenance task, releasing pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator.
